notes: visible: Expect.toBeVisible; hidden: Expect.toBeHidden (also succeeds for no matches). Use locator.first for non-strict selector visible/hidden waits, and the full locator for strict waits. attached: Expect.toHaveCount(1) on locator.first; detached: Expect.toHaveCount(0) on the full locator. These expectations retry until the condition holds; Locator.count alone is an immediate read, not a wait. For a strict single-match attached wait, use toHaveCount(1) on the full locator, but it retries multiple matches instead of immediately throwing Playwright strict-mode errors. Hidden/count expectations also do not reproduce every strict-mode failure. Non-strict selector waits can select the first match; disappearance waits require zero matches, not merely a hidden first match. Compositions return no retained ElementHandle: lazy locators re-resolve, so fixed element/subtree identity and handle-return semantics are not provided.

audit.scope: Pinned params.md wait-for-selector-state and class-locator.md waitFor compared with engine Visible, Hidden and Count expectations. Count expectations provide presence/absence waits; no exact strict-error or retained-handle equivalence is claimed.
